principles: The in-scope/exception boundary is authoritative per the existing guard test B-3cca branding rule; do not invent a new standard.
Minimal disruption: keep process-lane names / legacy alias / .koala runtime paths / salts / test-assertion intent, so build+e2e+validate stay green.
Gate-driven acceptance: story 4 extends the branding audit scope from 4 files to full active scope as a verify gate; story 3 cleans until the gate is green.
Batched and verifiable: by lab -> utils -> scripts -> main src -> main tests -> docs, each batch passes tests before moving on.
drivers: Remove user-readable koala branding before OSS (ship-clean program story 3).
Do not break established decisions (B-3cca process-lane keep) or the existing e2e test suite.
No collision/rework with the concurrent B-ed70 (lab/.Codex) and the 7-story environment.

options.name: A: semantic-full + extend branding gate
pros: Reuses the B-3cca established rule as the decision boundary; risk-controlled, does not break existing tests.
Cleans all user-readable branding (comments/@title/CLI prose/errors/prose/function names/temp prefixes).
Story 4 naturally lands as the 'extend branding audit scope' verify gate; both stories have real substance.
cons: Still 272 files / 1655 lines of line-by-line judgment; large effort, needs batching.
Kept items like process-lane names mean git grep -i koala is not fully 0 (but explained by the whitelist).

options.name: B: literal-full
pros: Most thorough; git grep -i koala theoretically 0.
cons: Overturns the B-3cca established process-lane keep decision.
Requires rewriting many e2e tests and changing dispatch/agent type registration; highest collision and rework risk.

options.name: C: narrow prose+comments only
pros: Fastest and safest; does not touch tests/scripts.
cons: koala branding remains in scripts and tests; the verify gate cannot be fully green.

rationale: After the precise inventory the user explicitly chose option A. Reusing the existing guard test B-3cca's classification rules as the in-scope/exception boundary is risk-controlled and does not break existing tests or established decisions; story 4 naturally lands as the verify gate extending the branding audit scope to full active scope. Option B overturns an established decision and requires rewriting many tests; option C leaves script/test branding and the gate cannot be fully green; both rejected.

preMortem.scenario: Changing branding in test fixtures (runKoala* function names, mkdtemp prefix koala-*, koala.config.json fixtures) breaks e2e tests
preMortem.trigger: Renamed a function but missed a reference, or changed an assertion-intent fixture's koala literal
preMortem.consequence: npm run test:e2e fails, story stuck in TEST
preMortem.mitigation: Judge line-by-line with the B-3cca rule: assertNotContains(...,'koala...') keeps the literal; when renaming function names/temp prefixes, update all references; run lattice validate + e2e after each batch

preMortem.scenario: Accidentally renaming process-lane names (koala-codex / koala-review* etc.) breaks dispatch / agent type registration
preMortem.trigger: Did not follow the branding NEUTRAL_TOKEN_PATTERNS and changed process-lane names too
preMortem.consequence: dispatch cannot find the agent type; e2e / real-machine dispatch fails
preMortem.mitigation: Strictly follow the B-3cca rule and leave process-lane names; the extended branding gate + e2e double-check; before DEV, use a perl replica of the rule to generate the must-change list, which excludes process-lane names

preMortem.scenario: Collision with the concurrent B-ed70 in packages/lab/src/core/config.ts and lab/package.json
preMortem.trigger: This story changed the same spot B-ed70 is changing
preMortem.consequence: DONE merge conflict requiring manual rebase
preMortem.mitigation: Leave lab/package.json description and the config.ts .Codex line to B-ed70; this story only changes lab's other files; rebase main before DONE to check conflicts

preMortem.scenario: After extending the branding gate to full active scope, kept koala (.koala paths in tests, koala.config.json fixtures) is misclassified as unclassified, making the gate permanently red
preMortem.trigger: Extended the audit scope but did not extend the NEUTRAL_TOKEN_PATTERNS contextual exemptions
preMortem.consequence: story 4 verify gate cannot go green, blocking DONE
preMortem.mitigation: When story 4 extends the gate, also extend the exemptions (.koala paths in test context, koala.config.json assertion fixtures); first make the gate green against the post-cleanup state

preMortem.scenario: 1655 lines is large; a single session cannot finish, leaving a half-changed state
preMortem.consequence: worktree in a partially-renamed, tests-red intermediate state
preMortem.mitigation: Batch by directory/category, run tests and commit after each batch (Lattice checklist tracks progress); worktree + Lattice story are recoverable, session_brief resumes
